evidence_items.locator: Satya Nadella prepared remarks, infrastructure section

receipt.public_excerpt: All up, we added another gigawatt of capacity this quarter, and remain on track to double our overall footprint in just two years.

evidence_items.explanation: This is the wording he disputes. Microsoft says it "added" a gigawatt but does not say whether it was energized and in use, so it cannot settle the dispute.

receipt.public_excerpt: All up, we added nearly 1 GW of total capacity this quarter alone.

evidence_items.explanation: The prior-quarter statement that "another" refers back to. It uses the same undefined term.

evidence_items.locator: Satya Nadella prepared remarks, AI platform and infrastructure section

receipt.public_excerpt: We added 31 new datacenters across 5 continents this quarter, bringing the total to 88 this year

evidence_items.explanation: Implies 57 data centers were added in the first three fiscal quarters. But Microsoft gave no locations, megawatts per site, or energization status, so this does not show how much became live in January to March 2026.

receipt.public_excerpt: Microsoft SAT14,2026-03-31,"Building 2 fully operational, Building 1 expanded. Construction is already visibly complete.

evidence_items.explanation: Independent tracking shows at least one Microsoft site that is not Fairwater became fully operational in the quarter (IT power rising from 19 MW to 47 MW per Epoch). Epoch covers only part of Microsoft's footprint and none of its leased neocloud capacity, so it cannot confirm or refute a quarterly total near 1 GW.

unresolved_gaps: Microsoft does not publish energized or in-service megawatts by quarter, or define "added capacity".
No independent tally covers Microsoft's whole owned and leased footprint for January to March 2026.
Epoch's site tracker covers only some Microsoft sites and excludes most leased third-party capacity.
